reviewed_arguments: The cylinder extension uses the actual original coefficient families composed with a bounded normal retraction; the leading bundle map is retained and ellipticity is uniform.
Finite nested chart supports and a base retraction give exact complete local models. The raw matrix inverse bound has explicit constants before conversion to the mixed weight.

The actual coordinate kernel, density Jacobian and distinct source/target frame factors are retained. Compact amplitude reduction proves all real mixed orders, both normal tails and every differentiated remainder.
The finite square-partition operator is proper and its full coefficient operators include every tangential smoothing contribution. Its leading coefficient is the original bundle inverse.
Both localized model equalities are exact. The two global product decompositions keep all cutoff terms; complete paired commutator estimates give both degree minus one errors.
Previously proved actual finite correction now applies globally. The ordered difference identity proves choice independence precisely modulo degree minus m minus N for a fixed cylinder operator.

Every real two-weight Sobolev norm is compatible across preferred charts. The proof splits the localized conjugate from the full separated output tail, proves its differentiated normal estimates and rapid tangential decay including unbounded output, and bounds both pieces before applying the inverse transfer. Completeness, density, separated-kernel mapping and uniform full-cylinder error gains follow.
Returning to the original collar keeps every normal cutoff derivative. Global order minus one cutoff terms vanish only under the stated two-sided localization, where degree minus N holds.
Four whole solutions verify the first corrected coefficient, retained cutoff errors, variable leading-coefficient commutator and an exact singular-kernel obstruction to changing the collar.
The support diagram gives explicit admissible interval bounds, not cutoff value graphs. Half-space maps, supported-source jets, one-sided traces and U051 integration remain future analytic steps.
